role.altitude: The camera operator keeps choosing kit, building sets, reading shot lists, watching takes and directing in the studio; booking equipment by mail, hunting for the day's papers, noting problem takes and retyping running orders shrink a little.
skills_to_grow: Using the booking tool and shared call sheets
role.ambitious_version: A camera operator who arrives with the right kit and the day's plan on their phone and spends the time on the picture.

tasks.short: Select cameras, film stock, audio and lighting equipment for the filming, book them from the store, assemble studio sets and arrange the equipment, and check the equipment back in.

steps.what: Camera operator selects cameras, film stock, audio and lighting equipment for the filming
Camera operator checks availability and books the equipment from the store
Camera operator assembles studio sets and arranges cameras and lighting
Camera operator checks the equipment back in

tasks.design: Equipment is booked in a booking tool that shows what is free on the shoot date, instead of mailing the store. Items carry barcodes and are scanned out and back in. Choosing kit and building the set stay hands-on.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bookings went by mail and paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Equipment booking tools with barcode scanning.
tasks.still_hard: Last-minute changes to the shot list.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the lens that gives the look the director wants.

evidence.claim: Asset registers and booking tools replace equipment spreadsheets and mail.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing equipment and sets; filming is outside.
Choosing and building keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether the store already uses a booking tool.
research_questions: Do missing items on set fall?

incremental.description: Camera operator labels own or new equipment.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one fixed studio kit; high: many shoots with changing kit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find the work order, call sheet and shot list, read and analyze work orders and specifications to determine locations, procedures, sequences and setups, clarify questions and write setup notes.

steps.what: Camera operator finds the work order, call sheet and shot list for the day
Camera operator reads and analyzes work orders and specifications to determine locations, sequences of operations and camera setups
Camera operator clarifies questions with the director of photography
Camera operator writes setup notes with camera settings per setup

tasks.design: The production publishes the call sheet, shot list and work order for each day in a shared production tool, always the latest version, instead of mailing attachments. Reading and planning the setups stay with the camera operator. Setup notes use a short template on the phone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Call sheets came as mail attachments in several versions.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared production tools with current call sheets.
tasks.still_hard: Locations that differ from the plan.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing how a shot will cut with the next one.

evidence.claim: Shot lists and call sheets in spreadsheets and mail are the glue today.

assumptions: Boundary: understanding the day's work; filming is outside.
Input contract for s1: the production coordinator publishes each day's papers in the production tool.
Reading and clarifying keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether productions use a shared tool.
research_questions: Do setups from outdated papers stop?

incremental.description: Camera operator reports missing information in the production tool.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one studio with fixed routines; high: many locations and versions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: View films and playback to find problems of exposure, camera movement and subject distance, mark problem takes, resolve problems by deciding corrections and discuss them with the director.

steps.what: Camera operator views films and playback to find problems of exposure, camera movement and subject distance
Camera operator notes problem takes with timecode in the camera report
Camera operator resolves the problems: decides corrections to exposure control, movement and distance
Camera operator discusses the corrections with the director

tasks.design: Viewing takes and deciding corrections stay with the camera operator. Problem takes are marked with one tap in a camera report app that takes the timecode from the camera, instead of writing it on paper, and the editor sees the marks.
tasks.enabler_now: Camera report apps that read timecode.
tasks.still_hard: Problems that only show on a large screen.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a shot is technically fine but feels wrong.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in judging the picture.

reach.learn: Whether marked takes save time in the edit.

evidence.claim: Editing tools can match takes to the script and stack alternates, but give a rough cut, not a finished edit.

assumptions: Boundary: judging takes on set; editing is outside.
Viewing and deciding keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether cameras send timecode to the app.
research_questions: Do editors find usable takes faster?

incremental.description: Camera operator pairs the app with the camera each day.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few problem takes; high: long shoot days with many takes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the camera script from the running order, brief the camera team and presenters, direct studio productions by calling shots and cues, and review the recording.

steps.what: Camera operator prepares the camera script from the running order
Camera operator briefs the camera team and presenters
Camera operator directs studio productions: calls shots and cues
Camera operator reviews the recording and notes fixes

tasks.design: The camera script starts from the running order in the newsroom or rundown system, with items, durations and presenters already in place, and the camera operator adds shots and cameras. Briefing, directing and reviewing stay fully human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Running orders were retyped into camera scripts.
tasks.enabler_now: Rundown systems that export to script templates.
tasks.human_edge: Timing a cut to a reaction.

reach.learn: Whether late changes reach the camera script.

evidence.claim: Reports and scripts can be produced from the playout and schedule data instead of retyping.

assumptions: Boundary: directing a studio production; editing is outside.
Input contract for s1: the producer keeps the running order in the rundown system.
Briefing, directing and reviewing keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether a rundown system is used.
research_questions: Do script errors in live shows fall?

incremental.description: Camera operator keeps the camera script template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short shows; high: long shows with many items.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
